title.narrative: Activity under preparation Boosting Sustainable Trade in Kenya

description.narrative: The Action aims to increase EU¿Kenya trade, both imports and exports, by improving the competitiveness and sustainability of Kenya¿s export sectors and reducing the carbon footprint of trade logistics.Specific Objective 1 (SO1) is to strengthen competitiveness by improving the consistency and availability of export produce while promoting value addition. Its outputs focus on increasing the sustainable and reliable supply of fresh produce and expanding value addition in selected value chains. Activities will support climate-smart production, post-harvest handling, standards and certification, inclusive business models, processing, circular economy innovation, and investment and market linkages.Specific Objective 2 (SO2) is to reduce the carbon footprint of exports by promoting a modal shift from air to sea freight. Its outputs include improved sea freight logistics capacity and more streamlined and transparent trade systems and procedures. These will be supported by firm-level cold chain and logistics upgrades, implementation of the Air-to-Sea Masterplan, digitalisation of SPS and customs procedures, and simplification of export regulations through risk-based controls. Together, these measures are expected to make exports more competitive and sustainable, while enabling a targeted shift of up to 50% of horticulture exports from air to sea. This will contribute to the long-term objective of expanding and greening EU¿Kenya trade.The Action is part of a broader Team Europe approach. It is explicitly linked to the Team Europe Initiatives on the Green Deal and the Northern Corridor, as well as to the EU¿s Global Gateway investments, which aim to transform the Northern Corridor from a basic transport route into a modern, green, and digitally enabled trade corridor. The Action focuses on first-mile supply, farm-level cold chain, and sea freight readiness in Kenya, thereby complementing the regional programme ¿Facilitating Trade and Infrastructure for Agro-Logistics and Cool Chain Development along the Northern Corridor¿, which addresses regional infrastructure and border facilities. It will also align with Team Europe¿s digitalisation agenda, recognising that trade digitalisation and corridor data systems are essential to reducing delays, losses, and costs in perishable exports. In addition, it is expected to mobilise and align contributions from EU institutions and Member States around green, digital, and trade-connectivity investments under the Global Gateway framework.
